patch.value:
## Rationale

The portfolio has six deadlined outcome milestones (pm-j82fd3, pm-9rgaal, pm-w7ccmv, pm-o87av6, pm-xp1xsw, pm-t4d7nz) and a promotion policy (pm-m08hza) that demands evidence-gated movement. Nothing computes whether those deadlines are achievable. Deadlines are asserted; they are never checked against the throughput the workspace has actually demonstrated.

pm-pee5 delivers descriptive flow metrics — cycle time, lead time, throughput, aging WIP — i.e. what already happened. This item is the predictive half: given recorded throughput, the open dependency graph, and per-item size signals, produce a calibrated distribution over completion dates and keep score on whether those forecasts came true.

Deterministic single-point estimates (sum of `estimated_minutes`) are the anti-pattern this replaces: they ignore variance, dependency serialization, and the empirical fact that estimates are biased.

## Method

1. **Empirical throughput sampling.** Sample completed-items-per-period from immutable history (`close` events with real completion time — see pm-bwnclq for completion-vs-tracker-close separation). No distribution assumption; the workspace's own record is the distribution.
2. **Monte Carlo over the dependency graph.** Draw throughput samples, walk the remaining scope in topological order over `blocked_by`/`parent` edges (pm-7ob5 critical path, pm-bzmeaa reachability), and emit a completion-date distribution per milestone. Report P50/P85/P95, not a date.
3. **Reference-class conditioning.** Condition samples on type/tag/parent class so a Chore-heavy remainder is not forecast with Feature-shaped throughput; back off to the global class when a class has too few samples (the same hierarchical shrinkage as pm-4k6b catalog algorithm (21) — small workspaces get wide, honest intervals instead of a special path).
4. **Scope-growth modeling.** Forecast against a scope that grows: measure the historical rate at which new items enter a milestone's subtree and sample it as a random variable. A forecast that assumes fixed scope is wrong by construction in a living backlog.
5. **Calibration ledger.** Every published forecast is recorded; when the milestone closes, the realized date is scored against the interval. Publish the hit rate. An uncalibrated forecast is worse than none, and only a recorded track record can prove calibration.

## Delivery

SDK primitives (sampling, simulation, calibration scoring) plus a package surface — extends the existing `pm-brief` reporting package alongside pm-pee5 rather than adding a core command or a new package. Raw simulation rows available as NDJSON for jq pipelines.

## Explicit non-goals

- No estimate-based critical-chain scheduling: `estimated_minutes` is an input signal, never the forecast basis.
- No resource/capacity modeling of agents — fleet allocation is pm-3oqjnc.
- No per-item due-date prediction surfaced as a promise; the unit of forecast is a milestone or subtree.
Probabilistic delivery forecasting: calibrated completion-date distributions for every milestone, sampled from recorded throughput and the dependency graph

Monte Carlo forecasting over empirical throughput, the open dependency graph, reference-class conditioning, and modeled scope growth, producing P50/P85/P95 completion ranges per milestone plus a calibration ledger that scores every past forecast against what actually happened.

Forecasts are computed from immutable history alone (throughput sampled from real completion events, never from estimated_minutes as a basis); output is a distribution with P50/P85/P95 per milestone or subtree, never a single date; the simulation walks blocked_by/parent edges so dependency serialization is reflected; sampling is conditioned by reference class (type/tag/parent) with documented back-off to the global class when a class is sparse; modeled scope growth is included as a sampled variable; every published forecast is recorded and scored against the realized outcome, and the calibration hit rate is queryable; raw simulation rows are available as NDJSON for jq; computation is built on promoted SDK primitives and surfaced through the existing pm-brief package, adding no core command

value.text: Forecasting refinement: use recorded completion throughput grouped by a declared reference class with sparse-data backoff; sample scope growth and dependency serialization independently. Publish P50/P85/P95 plus calibration coverage and the population window; never convert estimates into observed throughput. Use deterministic latest-start/slack computation as a separate consistency oracle and retain unschedulable residuals. Forecasts bind to a graph/history epoch and are scored when outcomes resolve. A date is a distribution-backed forecast, not a commitment created to deepen the graph.
